text:
Yes, a 20,000 mAh power bank is allowed on a flight, but only in your carry-on.

**The math:** The FAA says to divide mAh by 1,000 to get Ah, then multiply by the voltage. Most power banks use 3.7 V cells, so 20 Ah × 3.7 V ≈ 74 Wh. That is under the 100 Wh limit for spare lithium-ion batteries. Check the Wh rating printed on your bank if it has one. ([FAA: Airline Passengers and Batteries](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/airline-passengers-and-batteries))

**Rules to follow:**
- **Carry-on only.** Power banks are prohibited in checked bags. If your carry-on is gate-checked, take the power bank out and keep it with you in the cabin. ([FAA: Lithium Batteries](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/more_info/?hazmat=7))
- **Protect the terminals.** Keep it in its retail packaging, a pouch, or a case, or tape over exposed terminals, so they can't touch metal.
- **Don't bring a damaged or recalled unit.** Swollen or damaged batteries must not go on the plane.
- **Check your airline.** Some airlines and international carriers set stricter limits, including on how many power banks you can bring. ([IATA: Safe Travel with Lithium Batteries](https://www.iata.org/en/youandiata/travelers/batteries/))
- **If it overheats, smokes, or swells in flight,** tell the crew right away.

Banks over 100 Wh (up to 160 Wh) need airline approval, with a limit of two. Anything over 160 Wh is not allowed on passenger aircraft. ([FAA: PackSafe for Passengers](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe?packsafeq=power+bank))

If you're shopping for one, the [Baseus Blade H1 (20,000 mAh, 100 W)](https://dealectric.com/baseus-blade-h1-100w-20000mah) is listed at about 74 Wh and $89.99 as of 2026-10-21. That page is an affiliate site, so it may earn a commission if you buy through it.
